messages:
sana: Heads-up: ap-south1 slice-D reporting slow short-gen p50 creeping up over the last hour. Not a single spike but a steady drift from ~180ms -> ~420ms.
diego: Any noisy neighbor traces? GPU stalls or disk churn?
sana: Disk write amplification and increased agent CPU. Correlates to large parallel prefill tasks from tenant-flare that kicked at 08:02 IST.
marcus: tenant-flare onboarding uses 64 parallel workers by default; that's... ambitious for shared slices. Two options: ask them to throttle or use admission control at proxy to limit prefill concurrency.
ops-bot: prefill-orch: tenant-flare started prefill (64 workers) at 08:02:11. Retry policy 2/3.
sana: I'd prefer an infra-side soft mitigation first — admission-control + egress shaping that limits prefill traffic but keeps production traffic full-speed.
diego: Agreed. We have a new admission rule engine that can throttle based on route tags. We can apply a policy: for requests with header X-Onboard-Prefill -> concurrency cap 8 and token delay 100ms. That should cut back parallel writes.
marcus: If admission control isn't enough, fallback is to migrate prefill pods to a warmpool within the region or a dedicated ephemeral slice for onboarding traffic. Finance note: ephemeral dedicated still counts as reserved for billing period. finance-bot: estimated cost for ephemeral dedicated (slice-D small) ~ $650/day; warmpool fractional carve ~ $110/day at 15%.
sana: Let's try admission control + net shaping first. Diego, can you stage the policy as dry-run?
diego: running dry-run now. Commands: ```
admissionctl policy add --name prefill-throttle-tenant-flare --match-header X-Onboard-Prefill --concurrency 8 --token-delay 100ms --mode dry-run
netctl shape --tenant tenant-flare --egress 20mbps --burst 5mb --dry-run
monitorctl watch --metric p50_gen_ms --window 5m --expected-drop 30pct
```
diego: dry-run output: policy would cap ~72% of prefill concurrency, net shape wouuld limit sustained egress. No conflicts.
marcus: OK commit both but leave admission policy in permissive log mode for 2 minutes before enforcing. Need signal to rollback if synthetic traffic breaks their onboarding.
ops-bot: staging policy: prefill-throttle-tenant-flare (dry-run) created at 08:12:03.
diego: committing now. admissionctl set --mode enforce after 120s if no alerts.
(2m later)
sana: enforcement on. seeing concurrent prefill workers drop from 64 -> 9 within 30s. nvme write latency down ~x4. p50_gen_ms trending to ~210ms.
marcus: nice. Any sign they hit timeouts in their onboarding flow?
ops-bot: health-check: tenant-flare onboarding jobs still reporting progress, retry rate unchanged.
finance-bot: current mitigation adds negligible infra cost. If we need warmpool carve next 24h estimate ~$110. If escalate to ephemeral dedicated, ping for approval.
sana: Will keep admission policy for 60m then re-evaluate with tenant. Post-action: ask product to add onboarding-concurrency guardrails in the SDK defaults. Also propose an automated prefill admission rule per-tenant when prefill_rate > threshold for >2m.
marcus: Filing follow-up ticket with telemetry snapshots and suggested SDK patch. tagging @tenant-flare for coordination. :wave:
